Lying about PS2 image output

As it turns out, Linneman likes to post "real", rather than emulated, photos of console games. He tends to focus on 6th gen consoles.

He uses an XRGB mini. Yet, the GameCube, Xbox and Dreamcast all output at native 480p in a majority of their games, thus the XRGB mini is worthless for them. Baseline: XRGB isn't going to help these consoles because their native res is as good, or better than, the upscale. In fact, the XRGB could make them look worse than their native signals.

The PS2, on the other hand, is known for a rather unfortunate 480i signal in the majority of its releases. The XRGB mini upscale here would be tremendously helpful. And this is where Linneman focuses most of his posts: trying to "prove" that the PS2's image output is as good (or better!) than the Xbox, Dreamcast or GameCube.

First, a background on XRGB mini and what it is:

http://junkerhq.net/xrgb/index.php/XRGB-mini_FRAMEMEISTER

Upscaling settings for PS2:

http://junkerhq.net/xrgb/index.php/Playstation_2

And here's why it is useful for PS2, while being useless, at best, for Xbox (read the first few posts):

http://shmups.system11.org/viewtopic.php?f=6&t=33450&start=2640

Deinterlacing the signal is something any modern tv will do. Deinterlaced composite looks awful. Linneman knows this, which is why he bought a $500 device to help the PS2's image output; the XRGB mini explicitly exists to get the PS2 closer to the native component and VGA outputs of Xbox, GameCube and DC.

XRGB mini has poor component-in, however, so it may make Xbox games look worse than their native output. Yet Linneman runs the Xbox through it for comparative screen shots.

Can we please stop calling it Backwards Compatibility? You can't just shove an Xbox 360 game into the Xbox One and it'll play - it's emulation. Previously released titles for 6th and 7th gen Xbox consoles and their runtime binaries are repackaged with an emulator, and then added to the "backwards compatibility" catalogue. This is why it takes them so long to support all the older titles - because they have to fine-tune an emulator that's packaged with the re-release for each game, separately. It is also why they're being extremely selective.

Please note I have nothing against emulation or backwards compatibility. Anything to preserve old games is a welcome thing. I just find the constant use of this term completely disingenuous and straight up wrong. It's not backwards compatibility. Stop calling it that. This is more of a message towards the gaming press than it is to us gamers, really, though.
